gap: No result ChatGPT got sets each BLUETTI model's UPS switchover time against the 17 ms hold-up that Intel's ATX12V guide requires of a desktop PC power supply at full load. Elite 30 V2 (≤10 ms), Elite 100 V2 (10 ms) and Elite 200 V2 (15 ms) all come in under 17 ms. The AC180's 20 ms is 3 ms over, and the Apex 300 reaches 0 ms only on two front outlets in one voltage setup.
standout_why: I compared against the two pages ChatGPT cited. OutdoorGearLab's AC180 review gives the 20 ms cut-off and says the reviewer 'would hesitate to use it as a UPS for sensitive electronics', but it never ties that to any PC power-supply figure or compares other BLUETTI models. The CNET/Yahoo Tech page returned HTTP 403, so I couldn't check it. ChatGPT's answer itself names no switchover times and no hold-up figure. Our current page also lacks them. None of these pages explains that the Apex 300's 0 ms depends on the outlet and voltage mode.
decides: This confirms the Elite 100 V2 over the AC180 for anyone who wants a PC, NAS or router to stay up through a power cut. Both cost $499 at bluettipower.com today, but the Elite 100 V2 switches in 10 ms against 20 ms. The Elite 30 V2 at ≤10 ms is the small desk-UPS pick. For a large unit, the Elite 200 V2 at 15 ms is still inside 17 ms, and StorageReview found its switchover caused no reboots on running servers. Apex 300 buyers counting on 0 ms must use the two left front outlets in 240 V mode on a 120 V input. In 120 V mode StorageReview measured a 16 ms transfer.

findings.label: Desktop PC power supply hold-up after AC loss (Intel ATX12V Power Supply Design Guide v2.0, section 3.2.11)
findings.value: at least 17 ms at maximum continuous output load
findings.source_title: Intel ATX12V Power Supply Design Guide, Version 2.0, Voltage hold-up time
findings.note: Exact wording: the supply 'should maintain output regulation ... despite a loss of input power at the low-end nominal range—115 VAC / 57 Hz or 230 VAC / 47 Hz—at maximum continuous output load ... for a minimum of 17 ms.' This is a design-guide minimum at full load. Power supplies at light load usually hold up longer.

findings.note: Quote: 'BLUETTI's 0ms figure applies to two front outlets in 240V mode on a 120V input.' Kevin OBrien captured a 16 ms transfer with a Quarch capture on a Dell Pro Precision 9 T2. The workstation stayed up at about 100 W idle and again at about 700 W benchmark load. On a 240 V input in 240 V mode, every outlet gets the delay.
